Question B-006-010-009.

Why the correct answer is right: A 2 m mobile whip is far shorter than an 80-metre quarter wave, so it looks capacitive at that frequency. A series inductor, also called a loading coil, adds inductive reactance to bring it to resonance.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Use a solid radiating element instead of tubing": Changing from tubing to solid metal barely changes the electrical length. It does not supply the missing inductive reactance needed on 80 metres.
- sourceIndex 2: "Install a capacitor in series with the antenna": A short mobile whip already looks capacitive, so adding series capacitance is the wrong sign of reactance. It needs inductance.
- sourceIndex 3: "Connect the transmission line shield to the vehicle's chassis": Bonding the shield to the chassis helps provide a counterpoise, but it does not by itself cancel the capacitive reactance of a very short 80-metre whip.
